title: What Is The Carlsbad?? | Queens Gambit Declined | The Sensei Speedrun | GM Naroditsky

moves.spoken: The Carlsbad is defined by this early trade on d5 — instead of the traditional Bg5 main line with the pawn left on c4, we release the tension right away.

After Black recaptures we reach the Carlsbad structure: White's e-pawn against Black's c-pawn, with everything else symmetric. That small imbalance is what generates rich positional — and often sharply tactical — middlegame play.
We handle it like a normal Queen's Gambit Declined — the bishop to g5, e3, the standard moves — and let the structure dictate the game later.

Starting with the queen to c2 stops an annoying bishop to f5. When Black develops to the inaccurate d6 rather than e7, we go for the classic plan: install the Pillsbury Knight on e5, braced by the d4-pawn and a pawn to f4 — a construction many players simply can't handle. If Black challenges it, f5 nets a full minor piece for two pawns, and with our two bishops raking an open board we castle queenside and grind, seizing the only open file.

moves.spoken: The bishop to d6 is a long-known inaccuracy — the main line is the bishop to e7. Then the key choice is the knight to e2 versus f3: e2 leaves the f-pawn free for the f4 push behind the Pillsbury Knight.
